blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Watermark detectors decide whether one document came from a watermarked language model. Auditors often need a different number: the share of a corpus that did. We study this share for Gumbel-max and green-list (KGW) watermarks when every document may have been edited by an unknown amount. Without restrictions on the edits, the upper end of the identified set is 1. Combining a known least-favourable next-token distribution with a sequential coupling, we derive a power envelope indexed by three budgets: a retention floor, an entropy budget, and a budget for in-place substitutions, which for Gumbel-max make edited positions look less watermarked than human text. The envelope gives an identified set that is sharp for the alternatives it dominates, finite-sample bounds on the realized share of a fixed corpus with either the exact null or a null calibrated on an independent human sample, and confidence sequences for streams. In Gumbel-max simulations where the envelope binds, the bounds cover, and the threshold that maximizes the gap between envelope and null is generally as tight as twelve thresholds. On text from OPT-1.3B and Qwen3-1.7B, 12,000 fresh human documents scored under three keys show no robust departure from the exact null, and all bounds covered in resampling trials from finite pools of documents with random edits, substitutions and paraphrases; at a share of 0.2 the exact-null bound is about [0.14,0.38]. These results are fragile in two ways we make precise. LLM-paraphrased KGW pools fall below the envelope, yet at 2000 documents the bounds still covered in these trials. A simulated null error of 0.01, comparable to the largest deviation we observed at our thresholds, is likewise harmless at 2000 documents but breaks exact-null coverage at 100,000; a null calibrated on an independent human sample keeps coverage there, but needs a large reference sample to stay narrow.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Providers that watermark the output of their language models ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ; Aaronson, 2023 ; Kuditipudi et al., 2024 ; Dathathri et al., 2024 ) can test whether one text carries the watermark, and the statistical theory of such tests is well developed ( Li et al., 2025a ; Li et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) . Providers and the auditors they work with also face an aggregate question: what share of a collection of documents, such as submissions to a venue or posts on a platform, came from the watermarked model after users edited it? We call this the watermark-origin share . Two features of it shape everything below. It concerns one provider’s model, not machine-written text in general, because text from other models looks human to this test. And only the key holder can compute the statistics, so the analysis is run by the provider or by an auditor it gives access to.
blocks.zh: 标注其语言模型输出量的供应商(Kirchenbauer等,2023年;Aaronson等,2023年;Kuditipudi等,2024年;Datathri等,2024年)可以测试一个文本是否带有水印,而这种测试的统计理论也得到了完善(Li等,2025年a; 李等, 2026; 黄等, 2026). 提供商和他们与之合作的审计员也面临着一个总的问题:用户编辑后,从标有水印的模型中获得的文件,如提交地点或平台上的帖子,占文件汇编的多少? 我们称之为水印的股份。 它的两个特征塑造了下面的一切. 它涉及一个提供商的模型,而不是一般的机器写作文本,因为其他模型的文本看起来是人对这个测试. 并且只有钥匙持有者可以计算统计数据,因此分析由提供者或它允许访问的审计员进行.

blocks.en: The detection rate does not estimate this share. Human documents produce false positives, and watermarked documents that were edited, short or low in entropy are missed, by an amount that depends on how much each user edited. Correcting for the null rate, as Storey’s estimator does ( Storey, 2002 ) , removes the first error but not the second, and no point estimate says how wrong it might be. The share is only partially identified ( Manski, 2003 ) . Because human documents’ p p -values are uniform under a well-calibrated key, the corpus is a two-groups mixture with a known null; without restricting the alternative, the upper end of the identified set is 1 1 ( Genovese and Wasserman, 2004 ; Meinshausen and Rice, 2006 ) .

blocks.en: We restrict the alternative through the watermark mechanism and state the restriction as three budgets a user must choose: a floor ε min \varepsilon_{\min} on the share of positions that keep their watermark signal, a cap σ max \sigma_{\max} on in-place substitutions, and a cap δ \delta on next-token confidence. The resulting bounds are indexed by these budgets. Their lower end needs only a calibrated null. Their upper end needs the budgets, which cannot be estimated from the audited corpus, so we recommend reporting it over a range of budgets.

blocks.en: Han and Hashimoto (2026) argue, on privacy grounds, that watermarks should target aggregate usage rather than individuals. They design a sequence-level watermark with a randomized-response structure, in which each text contributes one bit, and give a clipped moment estimator of the corpus fraction with bias, variance and mean-squared-error bounds. Their scheme is sensitive to edits, which they leave to future work, and they give no intervals. Our results apply to the token-level schemes already deployed and allow every document to be edited. Li et al. (2025b) estimate the proportion ε \varepsilon of watermarked tokens within one mixed human–AI text, show that ε \varepsilon is identified for continuous pivots and not identified for the green-list pivot, and derive estimators that attain minimax lower bounds. Their results concern one document and do not include intervals. Blanchet et al. (2026) localize the token positions within a document where the watermark survives. Chai and Wang (2026) give matching sample-complexity bounds for estimating the Gumbel-max watermark proportion within one document, under the same non-degeneracy condition max w ⁡ P ⁡ ( w ) ≤ 1 − δ \max_{w}P(w)\leq 1-\delta that we use. Huang et al. (2026) , Su et al. (2026) and Luo et al. (2026) build anytime-valid tests from e-values and e-processes that accumulate evidence token by token within one text. Robustness of detection to paraphrasing and mixing has been studied empirically ( Krishna et al., 2023 ; Kirchenbauer et al., 2024 ; Piet et al., 2025 ) . Sander et al. (2024) ; Sander et al. (2025) aggregate watermark evidence over many texts to test whether a model was trained on watermarked outputs or whether a benchmark leaked into training, a different aggregate question from ours. Our unit of analysis is the document, our target is a corpus-level fraction, and our sequential procedures run across documents. They can take any of these per-document statistics as input. Liang et al. (2024a) ; Liang et al. (2024b) estimate the share of AI-modified text in corpora without watermarks, using a word-frequency mixture whose null must be estimated. Correcting a raw positive rate for imperfect sensitivity and specificity is classical in epidemiology ( Rogan and Gladen, 1978 ) , and bounds under misclassification or contamination are standard in econometrics ( Horowitz and Manski, 1995 ; Molinari, 2008 ) . Our upper bound is such a correction with a worst-case sensitivity that the watermark mechanism supplies. The exact null available with watermarks is what lets us state finite-sample guarantees. On the statistical side we use the two-groups model ( Storey, 2002 ; Genovese and Wasserman, 2004 ; Meinshausen and Rice, 2006 ) , partial identification ( Manski, 2003 ; Imbens and Manski, 2004 ) , and anytime-valid inference ( Ville, 1939 ; Howard et al., 2021 ; Ramdas et al., 2023 ; Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, 2024 ) . None of these tools is new here, and neither is the least-favourable NTP. The new part is the document-level envelope under unknown per-document edits, which converts the watermark mechanism and two interpretable budgets ( ε min , δ ) (\varepsilon_{\min},\delta) into a restriction on the alternative.

blocks.en: 2 Setup
blocks.zh: 2 设置

blocks.en: A language model with a finite vocabulary V V , | V | ≥ 2 |V|\geq 2 , produces a next-token distribution (NTP) P t P_{t} at each position t t . A watermark replaces ordinary sampling with a rule that uses pseudo-random numbers ζ t \zeta_{t} derived from a secret key and the preceding m m tokens. We consider two schemes. • Gumbel-max ( Aaronson, 2023 ) . ζ t = ( U t , w ) w ∈ V \zeta_{t}=(U_{t,w})_{w\in V} with independent U ⁡ ( 0 , 1 ) U(0,1) entries, the emitted token is w t = arg ⁡ max w ⁡ U t , w 1 / P t ​ ( w ) w_{t}=\arg\max_{w}U_{t,w}^{1/P_{t}(w)} , and the pivot is Y t = U t , w t Y_{t}=U_{t,w_{t}} . The rule samples exactly from P t P_{t} . • Green list ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ) . ζ t \zeta_{t} is a uniformly random subset Γ t ⊂ V \Gamma_{t}\subset V of size γ ​ | V | ∈ { 1 , … , | V | − 1 } \gamma|V|\in\{1,\dots,|V|-1\} , the logits of tokens in Γ t \Gamma_{t} are raised by b > 0 b>0 , and the pivot is Y t = 𝟏 { w t ∈ Γ t } Y_{t}=\mathbf{1}\{w_{t}\in\Gamma_{t}\} . blocks.en: Users edit generated text by different amounts, and edits act on pivots in three ways. A scored position whose token and context are both original keeps its dependence on the key. A position whose context was changed, by a deletion, an insertion or an earlier substitution, gets a new key draw; we assume such draws are previously unexposed and independent of the token, so its pivot is null. A position whose context is intact but whose token was replaced, by a substitution or an insertion, is different: its key draw is the one under which the original token won, so the new token is one that lost, and its pivot is smaller than a null pivot ( Lemma 2 ). Extending the hybrid-text model of Li et al. (2026) ; Li et al. blocks.en: We watermark OPT-1.3B ( Zhang et al., 2022 ) and Qwen3-1.7B ( Yang et al., 2025 ) with both schemes at temperature 1, with key-derived randomness seeded by SHA-256 of the key and the previous m = 3 m=3 tokens. KGW uses γ = 0.5 \gamma=0.5 and b = 2 b=2 . Prompts are the first 30 tokens of documents from the C4 validation split ( Raffel et al., 2020 ) . We generate up to 300 new tokens and keep documents with at least 50 new tokens, about 2000 per model and scheme. The analysis then drops documents with fewer than 50 scored positions, leaving between 1862 and 2011 unedited watermarked documents per model and scheme. At every position we log the unwatermarked NTP’s top probability max w ⁡ P t ​ ( w ) \max_{w}P_{t}(w) , which is the quantity that Definition 1 constrains. Human documents in the original batch are 4000 further C4 documents, truncated to 330 tokens and scored from position 30, the same offset as the generated text. Scoring deduplicates repeated contexts within a document. This removes 4.4 % 4.4\% to 4.7 % 4.7\% of positions in the original human batch and 3.4 % 3.4\% to 7.6 % 7.6\% in KGW text, but 34.5 % 34.5\% (Qwen3) to 44.6 % 44.6\% (OPT) in Gumbel-max text. With a fixed key and context hashing, a recurring three-token context reuses the same key draw, so when the NTP is also similar the same token tends to follow, and the text can fall into a loop. blocks.en: An earlier analysis, kept here because it shaped our conclusions, used a different design: i.i.d. labels, N = 4000 N=4000 , human documents resampled with replacement from the original 4000-document batch, and the narrower DKW band of Corollary 1 . For Qwen3 with KGW at π = 0.05 \pi=0.05 it covered in only 72 % 72\% of corpora. The same design with the fresh batch covers in 99.5 % 99.5\% , and Proposition 5 covers in 100 % 100\% with either batch; with Proposition 6 , five independent reference splits of the fresh batch all gave 100 % 100\% . The failure did not reproduce under the same key on the fresh batch, so it cannot be attributed to the key alone; an interaction between the key and the composition of the original batch is not ruled out. It was tied to the original human batch together with a design whose sampling slack is small. We read this as a warning, made precise in Section 5 : a null error of the size seen in the original batch is absorbed by the slack of a 2000-document corpus but not by that of a much larger one.

blocks.en: The watermark-origin share of a corpus is not identified without assumptions on how much signal survives editing, and no assumption on survival identifies it if next-token distributions may be point masses; nearly deterministic text makes the signal weak. With both, the watermark mechanism gives a power envelope, in closed form for KGW and computed conservatively for Gumbel-max, and the envelope gives bounds indexed by three budgets ( ε min , σ max , δ ) (\varepsilon_{\min},\sigma_{\max},\delta) . The lower end needs only a calibrated null. The upper end needs the budgets, which cannot be estimated from the audited corpus.

A key holder can check the document-level condition on its own generations under edits it can simulate, using the normalized ratio of Section 6 ; the relevant edits are those of real users, so this is a diagnostic, not a guarantee. A simple robustness device is a contamination share η \eta : if a fraction η \eta of watermarked documents may fall outside the class but is still at least as detectable as human text, the upper end becomes U / ( 1 − η ) U/(1-\eta) , and the smallest η \eta that moves the upper end past a decision threshold is a natural breakdown point ( Horowitz and Manski, 1995 ) . A single threshold chosen without data to maximize h low ​ ( t ) − t h_{\mathrm{low}}(t)-t is a reasonable default; in our simulations the multi-threshold bound was never far from the best single threshold, so it is a cheap guard against a poor choice. For monitoring, Theorem 2 needs no model of how adoption changes, but it still needs the exact null and the envelope conditionally on the past, and labels must not be chosen after seeing the document.

blocks.en: The guarantees are not adversarial. A user who paraphrases deliberately can push documents outside the class and make the upper end fail; text crafted to look watermarked (spoofing) would bias the lower end. Calibration must be redone when the key, the tokenizer, the decoding rule or the model changes. Post-trained models produce lower-entropy text than the base models we use, which makes detection harder ( Bahri and Wieting, 2026 ) and makes the entropy budget δ \delta more consequential.
blocks.zh: 这些保证不是对抗性的。 刻意作诠释的用户可以将文档推出类外并让上端出故障;被刻制出外观有水标记(spoofing)的文本会偏向下端. 当密钥,活化器,解码规则或模型发生变化时,校正必须被重接. 后受训练的模型产生出比我们使用的基准模型更下等的通体文字,这使得检测更加困难(Bahri and Wieting, 2026)并使得 en平预算 \\ delta 产生更大的结果.

blocks.en: The guarantees are relative to an edit model in which each position is retained, reset or substituted in place, independently given the past. LLM paraphrasing is outside that model, and the KGW paraphrase pools fall below the envelope at moderate thresholds; bounds that hold under paraphrasing would need a different restriction, for example on the semantic distance of the rewrite. Our random edits share token survivals between neighbouring positions, which the model does not describe exactly. The exact null is an assumption. Three keys and two batches of human text found no robust departure from it, but cannot rule out a key or domain effect below what twelve thousand documents detect, and the difference between our two human batches is unexplained. The calibrated null replaces this assumption with another: the reference sample must come from the same population as the human documents in the audited corpus, which is hard to guarantee when the corpus mixes domains. In our experiments corpora were drawn without replacement from finite pools, so coverage is conditional on those pools. The envelope must hold conditionally on length ( Assumption 2 ). Its numerical lower bound is conservative in exact arithmetic, and the floating-point error, checked against direct summation at selected lengths and lattice resolutions, was measured rather than proved small. Sharpness is with respect to the relaxed class. The experiments use two small open base models at temperature 1 1 , one context width, two schemes and synthetic mixtures. They do not cover instruction-tuned models, lower temperatures, low-entropy domains such as code, repeated-context masking at generation time, edits with a fixed count rather than a random share, or paraphrase pools larger than about 300 documents per model and scheme; these are the settings in which the envelope is most likely to fail. No corpus with known watermark prevalence is public, and deployed schemes such as SynthID ( Dathathri et al., 2024 ) keep their keys private. The method needs only per-document pivots, so it is available to any key holder.
blocks.zh: 这些保证是相对于编辑模型的,其中每个位置都保留、重新设置或替换,而独立地考虑到过去。 LLM 参数化位于该模型之外,KGW 参数化池在中度阈值下低于信封;在参数化下所持有的界限需要不同的限制,例如重写时的语义距离. 我们的随机编辑在相邻位置之间共享符号存活,模型对此没有准确描述. 完全无效是假设 三把钥匙和两批人文文字没有发现有力的偏离,但不能排除在一万二千个文件所探测到的下方的钥匙或域名效果,我们两批人文的区别是无法解释的. 校正后无效用另一个假设取代了这个假设:参考样本必须来自与被审计人体内人类文件相同的人群,这在被审计人混合领域时很难保证. 在我们的实验中 蝎子是没有替代 从有限的池, 所以覆盖条件 这些池。 信封必须有条件地以长度(假设2 )为条件。 它的数值下限在精确算术上是保守的,所测量的浮点误差与所选长度和纬度分辨率的直接总和相比是很小的。 锐利是针对放松的阶级. 实验使用两个温度为1 1 的小型开放基模型,一个上下文宽度,两个方案以及合成混合物. 它们不涵盖指令调制的模型,更低的温度,低调域,如代码,代代时的重复缩写,用固定的计数而不是随机的分数来编辑,或者每个模型和计划比大约300个文档大的一个参数集合;这些都是信封最有可能失败的设置. 任何已知有水印的装置都是公开的,而SynthID(Dathari等,2024年)等已部署的装置都保持其钥匙的保密。 这个方法只需要每个文件的活字片,所以它可供任何密钥持有人使用.

blocks.en: The construction follows the hedged capital process of Waudby-Smith and Ramdas (2024) . We use their predictable plug-in bets. Averaging over thresholds needs no multiplicity correction for validity, but it is not free: when one component alone drives rejection, it must reach about 2 ​ J / α 2J/\alpha . In return the data choose the most informative threshold. When computing C k C_{k} on a grid of π 0 \pi_{0} values we take an outer approximation. Because C k C_{k} is an interval, extending each end of the accepted grid points to the adjacent rejected grid point contains it. If no grid point is accepted at time k k , the interval C k C_{k} may still be nonempty between two grid points; we then skip the intersection at time k k , which only enlarges the running interval and keeps it valid. The running interval starts at [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] .
blocks.zh: 该建筑遵循了被套住的瓦乌德比-斯密斯和拉姆达斯(2024年)的资本流程. 我们用他们可预测的插入赌注。 超过阈值不需要多重校正的有效性,但它不是免费的:当一个组件单独驱动拒绝时,它必须达到约2 J / α 2J/\ alpha. 作为回报,数据选择了信息最丰富的阈值。 当计算 C k C_{k} 在 ^ 0\ pi_{0} 值时, 我们取一个外相值 。 因为Ck C_{k}是一个间隔,将所接受的网格点的每个端延伸至相邻被拒绝的网格点都包含它. 如果在 k k 时没有接受网格点, C k C_{k 的间隔可能仍然是两个网格点之间的非空; 然后在 k k 时跳过相交点, 它只会扩大运行的间隔并保持其有效 。 运行间隔起于 [0, 1] [0, 1].
